version.changelog: Add public sample record and clean source links.

llm.summary: This is a disclosed fitness-planning skill made of Markdown prompts, with no malicious code found, though it asks for health-related details and uses an unpinned install command users should review.

dimensions.detail: The artifact is Markdown-only and does not request local file access, credentials, background services, network calls during use, destructive actions, or broad indexing.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The documented install path uses npx and a mutable GitHub repository with --full-depth, which is a supply-chain integrity risk, but it is user-directed installation guidance rather than hidden runtime behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are scoped to eliciting a fitness profile, filling a record template, and producing conservative training decisions with MissingInputs; inspected comments and BOM markers do not contain prompt hijacking, system override, exfiltration, or deceptive directives.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The prompts refer to a reusable or stored FitnessProfile, but there is no instruction to write persistent agent memory, escalate privileges, install services, or retain data outside the user's chosen workflow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is constraint-aware workout planning, and its requests for goals, injuries, pain, equipment, time, and recovery fit that purpose; the health details are sensitive, so users should share only what is needed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, review the resolved repository contents and prefer a pinned commit or verified release instead of the mutable npx/GitHub command. When using the skill, avoid sharing unnecessary medical history and do not treat its output as diagnosis, rehabilitation care, or a substitute for a qualified clinician.
llm.findings:
[P2] unexpected: Inspection found UTF-8 BOM markers and visible HTML metadata comments at file starts; these describe file purpose and do not contain hidden malicious directives or evaluator-targeting instructions.
[SQP-2] expected: The skill asks about pain, injuries, medical prohibitions, and recovery because those are directly relevant to safer fitness planning; this remains sensitive health data and would benefit from clearer privacy and optionality language.
[SQP-3] expected: The package includes English and Chinese variants and links between them; I did not find a runtime requirement that forces a user's language against their preference.
[RP1] expected: The install command is a normal user-directed skill installation flow, but it is not pinned to an immutable CLI version or repository revision.
[T08] expected: The static supply-chain finding is supported for the documented installation path, but the audited artifact itself contains no executable payload, insecure dependency file, persistence mechanism, or credential access.
